senses.gloss: A state of doing something automatically, without thinking about it.
examples: I was so tired I drove home on *autopilot*.
After twenty years at the desk, she answers those calls on *autopilot*.
He sat through the whole meeting on *autopilot* and remembers none of it.

senses.gloss: A sudden flood of things arriving all at once.
examples: The story set off an *avalanche* of angry email.
She came back from vacation to an *avalanche* of paperwork.
An *avalanche* of orders came in the day the ad aired.

senses.gloss: A person who holds a first university degree, used mainly in the name of the degree itself.
examples: The job posting asks for a *bachelor*'s degree in accounting.
He finished his *Bachelor* of Arts in three years.
Both finalists hold *bachelor*'s degrees in nursing.

senses.gloss: The general situation or set of conditions against which events happen.
senses.ru: фон, общая обстановка (на фоне которой что-то происходит)
examples: The talks opened against a *backdrop* of rising tension.
The novel unfolds against the *backdrop* of the Depression.
Rising rents form the *backdrop* to the entire debate.

senses.gloss: A person's education, work experience, and family circumstances.
examples: She has a *background* in software engineering.
The company runs a *background* check on every new hire.
The students come from very different *backgrounds*.

senses.gloss: The facts and history a person needs in order to understand a present situation.
examples: Let me give you some *background* on the case before we start.
The article fills in the *background* to the strike.
The reporter asked for *background* off the record.

senses.gloss: The area close to where you live or operate, thought of as your own territory.
examples: Nobody wants a landfill in their own *backyard*.
The company found its best customers right in its own *backyard*.
The senator called the conflict a crisis in America's *backyard*.

senses.gloss: A situation or set of circumstances, especially one that has completely changed.
examples: Once the funding came through, it was a whole new *ballgame*.
Coaching high school and coaching college are two different *ballgames*.
With rates this high, buying a house is a different *ballgame*.

senses.gloss: A rough range within which an amount is expected to fall.
examples: Give me a *ballpark* for what the repairs will cost.
Your estimate is in the right *ballpark*.
Fifty thousand was in the *ballpark*, but the winning bid came in higher.

senses.gloss: The time and energy a person or team has available for something.
senses.ru: ресурс времени и сил, «пропускная способность» человека
examples: I don't have the *bandwidth* to take on another project this month.
Her team is out of *bandwidth* until the audit is done.
Do you have the *bandwidth* for a quick call this afternoon?

senses.gloss: A complete lack or collapse of something valued, such as honesty or ideas.
examples: Critics saw the decision as proof of the party's moral *bankruptcy*.
The book argues that the whole theory ended in intellectual *bankruptcy*.
He accused the network of complete ethical *bankruptcy*.

senses.gloss: Something that shows how a situation or a public mood is changing.
examples: Consumer spending is a good *barometer* of the economy.
Local elections often serve as a *barometer* of the national mood.
Ticket sales are the industry's *barometer* of what audiences want.

senses.gloss: A starting measurement that later results are compared against.
examples: The study used 2019 emissions as its *baseline*.
We need a *baseline* before we can measure any progress.
Reading scores came in ten points above the *baseline*.

senses.gloss: The line marking each end of a tennis or basketball court.
examples: She hit a forehand from well behind the *baseline*.
He drove along the *baseline* for an easy layup.
The serve landed just inside the *baseline*.

senses.gloss: The things a person owns, especially ones they carry or keep with them (used only in the plural).
examples: Please take all your *belongings* with you when you leave the train.
The fire destroyed most of their *belongings*.
She packed her *belongings* into two suitcases and moved out.

senses.gloss: The advantages or good effects that something produces.
examples: The *benefits* of regular exercise show up within a few weeks.
We weighed the costs against the *benefits* before deciding.
Tax cuts of that kind bring few *benefits* to renters.

senses.gloss: A sharp, harsh taste, like that of strong coffee or dark chocolate.
examples: A little sugar cuts the *bitterness* of the grapefruit.
These greens have a pleasant *bitterness* to them.
Roasting the beans too long adds *bitterness*.

senses.gloss: A temporary loss of consciousness or of memory.
examples: He had a *blackout* and woke up on the kitchen floor.
She has no memory of the drive home — a complete *blackout*.
The doctor asked whether he had ever had *blackouts* before.

senses.gloss: An official ban on reporting or releasing information.
examples: The army imposed a news *blackout* on the operation.
There was a media *blackout* until the families had been notified.
The company kept a total *blackout* on the merger talks.

senses.gloss: Approval or permission from someone whose opinion carries weight.
examples: The board gave the merger its *blessing*.
They married with her father's *blessing*.
He took the job without his family's *blessing*.

senses.gloss: Something you are lucky and grateful to have.
examples: Having good neighbors is a real *blessing*.
Losing that job turned out to be a *blessing* in disguise.
She told the kids to count their *blessings*.

senses.gloss: A tough lawn and pasture grass with a bluish-green color.
examples: He reseeded the front lawn with Kentucky *bluegrass*.
The pasture is mostly *bluegrass* and clover.
*Bluegrass* holds up well through a cold winter.

senses.gloss: A detailed plan for how something should be done.
examples: The report offers a *blueprint* for fixing the school system.
His campaign became a *blueprint* for other candidates.
The team had no *blueprint* for handling a crisis like this.
